---
title: Read or plot saved results
---

Start here when the analysis already exists. Read a full saved object, RDS,
workbook or delivery directory before requesting another fit.

## Read an existing delivery

```r
readback <- iobrcausal(
  request = list(operation = "read"),
  inputs = list(path = "results/my_delivery")
)
print(readback)
```

A direct R reader is also available:

```r
bundle <- iobr_causal_read_result_bundle("results/my_delivery")
iobr_causal_readout(bundle)
```

Directory discovery can be a bounded preview. Use the matching full numeric
table and companion files before reporting a specific feature's estimate.

## Draw a figure from saved numbers

When `saved_table` is a single numeric effect table:

```r
figure <- iobrcausal(
  request = list(operation = "plot", parameters = list(
    plot_type = "forest", formats = c("png", "pdf", "svg")
  )),
  inputs = list(result = saved_table), output_dir = "figures"
)
```

For a result object containing several endpoint tables, specify the matching
`table_path`. The plot operation uses saved estimates and intervals. A survival
curve additionally requires a saved curve cache; raw OS columns do not stand in
for cached curves.

Check the exported source table and `plot_provenance.csv` alongside each image.
Explicit Log-OR and Log-HR values may be exponentiated with their own intervals;
additive effects remain additive. A display subset retains the original family.

## Reuse and reproduction

Reuse a compatible saved result when the inputs and request are unchanged.
An explicit `reproduce` request is different: it can execute a fresh association
run using verified original inputs, seed and settings, then compare saved
scientific tables. Frozen OS mediation has its own reuse rules; see
[advanced analysis](../reference/advanced.qmd).
